ADR-0001 accepted as option B: herddash is a narrow complement, a headless recorder that persists every agent status transition with per-account attribution under bounded retention, with a minimal page and a read-only API, running beside devswha/herdr-web-ui rather than replacing it. Record: docs/adr/0001-what-herddash-is.md

Why: Hands-on evaluation of two existing browser UIs took three of the five claimed differentiators including the primary thesis; persisted history and per-account attribution are the only two that survive, and B keeps both plus the single-binary property without foreclosing a later upstream contribution.

text:
The board is the feature herddash is measured by: a notification center with one box per agent showing status, owning account and time waiting, sorted longest-waiting first; read-only, no terminal, no chat, no pane control. The recorder engine (subscribe, persist transitions, attribute, read-only API, event stream) is what makes the board trustworthy and feeds future surfaces. Corrects ADR-0001's consequence that the board is secondary; to be recorded as ADR-0003.

Why: The operator's daily value is glancing at the board in another window all day; a PRD that calls it secondary would produce epics that treat it as secondary, the success metric (noticing a waiting agent sooner than the toast) is a board metric, and the differentiator the operator believes in is restraint, a notification center rather than a browser client, which can only be defended if the board is the product being restrained.
